title: The finite-energy boundary of a group
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Functions of finite energy on the Cayley complex of a finitely presented group, and the boundary they give the group. The first lesson sets up the Cayley complex of a presentation with relators of length at most three, proves that cocycles are gradients, defines the Hilbert space of finite-energy gradients and its subspace generated by finitely supported functions, bounds the interaction of two level cuts, and, when the two spaces differ, constructs a function with connected level sides. The second lesson, for a one-ended Cayley graph, embeds the group in a cube by the translates of that function and by functions recording the components of boxes, and proves that the closure is a compact metric space in which the edges have square summable lengths, that its boundary is a continuum with more than one point, and that vertices near a boundary point are joined by paths near it. The third lesson proves that the group acts on this boundary as a convergence group, compares g and gp for a parabolic fixed point p, and shows that every orbit is dense when the group is torsion-free. The fourth lesson proves that the boundary has covering dimension at most one, and that its first Čech cohomology vanishes when every 1-cochain on the Cayley complex with finitely supported coboundary can be corrected by a finitely supported cochain; so under these assumptions the boundary is locally connected only if it has cut points. The fifth lesson treats the case in which the boundary has cut points: from the tree of cut points it constructs a block of the boundary, a compact connected subset without cut points onto which the boundary retracts, of dimension at most one and with vanishing first Čech cohomology. The sixth lesson collects, for the boundary without cut points and for a block alike, the properties of the continuum, of a graph accumulating on it and of the group acting on both that the later arguments use. The seventh lesson prepares two tools for the continuum without cut points: component labels of the graph after deleting vertices, which are locally constant on the continuum, and an invariant system of annuli with the depth function that counts nested annuli. The eighth lesson studies the vertices of the graph of depth at least a given number: translates of a closed set by elements of large depth shrink to a point of the continuum, depths measured from them add up with a bounded error, and after such a translation any two points of the continuum other than that point get the same component label. These are the first steps of OpenAI's proof (2026) of the Singer conjecture in dimension four outside the middle degree.
prerequisites: core course Functional Analysis (D20): closed subspaces of a Hilbert space, the Riesz representation theorem
core course Measure and Integration (D10): Tonelli's theorem, dominated convergence
free groups and presentations of groups
for the third lesson: the course Convergence groups (lesson Convergence actions and their elements)
for the fourth lesson: the course Continua, arcs and cut points, and covering dimension (Definition 2.1 of Covering dimension and finite trivializing covers)
for the fifth lesson: the course Convergence groups (lesson The tree of cut points) and, through it, the course Pretrees
the course proves every other fact it uses

checks.reading: Each proof was written out and re-read step by step on 11 Oct 2026 against Section 3 and Lemma found:gradient of OpenAI's preprint (library copy at commit adc7f124). Lesson 2 spells out the cases of degenerate cells in the count of components and the three properties of the small box in the proof of the path theorem. The exercises on Z, Z^2 and the free group were worked out by hand. Lesson 3 was written against Section 4 of the preprint; it adds a proof that a group with an infinite cyclic subgroup of finite index is not one-ended, and gives the constant 2 in the diameter bound. Lesson 4 was written against Section 5 of the preprint; it replaces Hausdorff measure by an elementary notion of length zero, states the cohomological hypothesis on the Cayley complex, works with any abelian coefficient group, and adds an exercise showing that the hypothesis fails for Z^2. Lesson 5 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Section 7 of the manuscript (lemmas block:graph and block:near-path, proposition block:retraction); every step was re-derived; no gap found. The lesson states as hypotheses the two properties of the group that the tree of cut points needs and that have no provider in the programme. Lesson 6 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the last part of Section 7 of the manuscript (proposition block:setting); each of the six properties was verified in both cases; no gap found. Lesson 7 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against Section 8 of the manuscript (lemmas ann:extension, ann:component, ann:system, ann:depth); every step was re-derived; no gap found. The extension across a point is taken from the lesson on Čech cohomology (Corollary 4.5). Lesson 8 was written on 12 Oct 2026 against the first half of Section 9 of the manuscript (lemmas push:shrinking, push:depth-comparison, push:component-labels, push:translated-deletions, push:eventual-labels); every step was re-derived; no gap found. Convergence of sets is stated without the Hausdorff metric (sets that shrink to a point).
checks.layout: Measured in the staged pages at column widths 1100, 768, 543 and 375 px on 11 and 12 Oct 2026: 3,876 formulas in the eight lessons, none wider than the column, no TeX errors.

open_obligations: The translation between assumption (C_k) of the fourth lesson and the vanishing of the group cohomology H^2(Gamma; k Gamma) is not proved in the programme; it belongs to a course on group cohomology with group-ring coefficients, which does not exist yet.
The link between D_0 != D and a positive first L^2-Betti number is not proved in the programme; it belongs to a course on L^2-invariants, which does not exist yet.

The fifth lesson assumes the two hypotheses of the lesson The tree of cut points (course Convergence groups) that have no provider in the programme: the fixed-point property for trees with finite edge stabilizers, and that the group fixes a point of the dendrite quotient of the boundary.
free_sources: OpenAI, The Singer conjecture in dimension four (OpenAI Math Release preprint, 25 Sep 2026), Sections 2 and 3
